purpose: Every wall-clock constant-time test in native/*/tests is classified here. tests/test_ct_audit_contract.py fails when a timing site is added, renamed or removed without updating this file, and when a secret_dataflow site is not covered by an ol_ct_audit case that names it.

classes.secret_dataflow: The measured function takes a secret. ol_ct_audit marks it secret and Memcheck proves no undeclassified branch or memory index depends on it in the release code generation.
classes.public_inputs: Every input the measured function branches on is public (signatures, public keys, displayed codes). Uniform timing across tamper positions is a robustness property, not a confidentiality claim; there is no secret for a dataflow audit to mark.
classes.test_local_reference: The timed code is defined in the test itself; no production code path runs it. Not evidence about shipped code.
classes.functional_guard: A semantic companion or an instrument self-test, not a timing claim.

sites.rationale: HMAC chain under the secret root key; the accept/reject branch is the declared verdict.

Passphrase, roots and check hashes are secret. DuressGate::decide is audited as uniform (no secret-dependent branch at all, not even a declassified one); DuressGate::open adds only the declared real/duress/rejected classification, which is not timing-uniform across outcomes by construction.

LayerKey equality through subtle::ConstantTimeEq.

The real IdentityBoundServerVerifier accepts the matching certificate and rejects a mismatch at every byte with the fingerprint error, so the timing comparison compares like with like.

The dialer's expected fingerprint is secret from a machine in the middle that presents certificates and times the rejection. Drives the production verifier (ol_quic::tls::verify_identity_cert). Until 2026-11-25 this test timed a comparator defined in the test itself; the production compare was a hand-written OR-fold and is now subtle::ConstantTimeEq.
